features.title: Process memory by workspace
features.summary: One page shows the resident memory of every process tree the threads started, grouped by workspace: live background jobs with their owning thread, other children of this Host, and detached trees still running inside a workspace after their parent exited, with the memory-pressure level and a confirmed stop per tree, per workspace, or for every detached tree. The sidebar entry carries a pressure dot and the detached total.
failureModes: A supervisor that launched this Host is an orphan inside a workspace too; it is never listed, so it can never be stopped from here.
A pid recycled between the snapshot and the stop is refused instead of signalling an unrelated process.
A job is stopped through the job registry so its Session records the kill; only trees no live job owns are signalled directly.
Orphans outside every workspace (apps, system agents, unrelated daemons) are not listed.
A platform without ps/lsof or /proc reports itself unsupported instead of an empty board.

externalDependencies.boundary: Read-only process table, working directories and memory-pressure level, run through the Host subprocess service; the only writes are the confirmed SIGTERM/SIGKILL of listed trees.
externalDependencies.deterministicFake: src/process-table.test.ts feeds parsed ps rows, working directories, workspaces, Sessions and live jobs to the pure snapshot builder.

externalDependencies.boundary: Read-only projection of live jobs to attribute process trees to their Session, plus the registry kill for a job tree.
externalDependencies.deterministicFake: src/process-table.test.ts passes live jobs as plain records with label, owner and start time.

verification.testName: accounts a job tree to its thread workspace and names the heaviest process
counts orphans inside a jj sibling checkout as detached and ignores orphans outside every workspace
never offers the supervisor that launched this Host as a detached tree
does not hand one job to two process trees started in the same second
orders a tree children first so a stop never leaves a parent to respawn a child
treats a systemd --user subreaper as the adopter of a detached tree
